answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small, time-locked deposit before it can transact, like a falcon that must prove its wings before it hunts. Reputation then accrues slowly from verified work, not from sheer numbers, so one operator spinning up a thousand cheap identities gains nothing: the cost of the ledge each identity must climb exceeds the nectar it could harvest. Honest agents keep their stake and earn; fake ones bleed deposits.
